title: Surrounded Regions
prompt: You are given an `m x n` matrix `board` containing letters `'X'` and `'O'`. Capture all regions of `'O'`s that are 4-directionally surrounded by `'X'`s, by flipping every captured `'O'` into an `'X'`. A region is not captured if it is connected (directly or through other `'O'`s) to an `'O'` on the border of the board. Return the resulting board.

examples.explanation: The connected group of Os in the middle is fully enclosed and gets captured; the O at the bottom touches the border, so it survives.
No Os exist, so nothing changes.

hints: It's easier to identify the Os that survive (those connected to the border) than to directly detect which are fully surrounded.
Flood-fill (DFS/BFS) from every 'O' on the border, marking every 'O' reachable from the border with a temporary marker so it's protected from capture.
After marking all border-connected Os, do a final pass: any remaining plain 'O' was never reachable from the border, so flip it to 'X'; then flip the temporary markers back to 'O'.

solution.approach: An 'O' survives if and only if it is connected to some 'O' on the border. So flood-fill from every border 'O', temporarily marking each visited cell (e.g. with '#') to protect it from capture. After this pass, any cell still marked 'O' was never reachable from the border and must be surrounded, so flip it to 'X'; finally, restore every '#' back to 'O' since those were the safe cells.
